slides.heading: Logical OR
slides.body: Logical OR is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Logical OR
slides.body: The or operator is True when at least one condition is True. It is useful when there are alternative ways to qualify.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: or is like using either cash or a card to pay. You only need one available option.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Check if a user is an admin or a moderator.

quiz.prompt_text: When does the "or" operator return True?

options: Only when both conditions are True
When at least one condition is True
Only when the second condition is True

quiz.explanation: Correct! The or operator returns True when at least one of the conditions is True. It only returns False when both are False.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to check if a user is an admin or a moderator.
quiz.explanation: Both variables must be assigned first, then the or expression checks whether at least one of them is True. Even though is_admin is False, the result is True because is_moderator is True.

quiz.prompt_text: Check if is_admin or is_moderator is True and print the result.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(is_admin or is_moderator) outputs True because is_moderator is True. The or operator only needs one True condition to return True.
